title: Why 4 + 3 Is Not 7: 2D Motion Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Aarav cuts across an empty road at a slant: every second, 4 m east and 3 m north. Is he going at 7 m/s? Most people say yes, and they are wrong. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 3, Motion in a Plane) we learn the one trick behind all motion in a plane: it is two straight line motions happening at the same time.

On a live motion notebook we watch the x and y shadows of a moving point, freeze it in a slow-mo replay and build the velocity vector from vx and vy. We derive v = vx i + vy j, the speed as the square root of vx squared plus vy squared, and tan theta = vy / vx. Then a marble on a tilted board shows constant acceleration in a plane, and we use the straight line equations twice, along x and along y. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example, the exam trap of adding vectors like numbers, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 A kite, a ball, a bicycle: motion that bends
0:28 Position in a plane: x, y and the position vector
0:50 Motion notebook: two shadows, one diagonal
1:38 The rules: velocity, speed and direction
2:19 Adding acceleration: a marble on a tilted board
2:46 The equations of motion, used twice
3:15 Side by side + pause and think
3:45 Worked example
4:24 Exam trap: adding vectors like numbers
4:48 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:29 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Projectile Motion. Throw one ball sideways and drop another: which lands first?
